definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese wooden sandals with an elevated base supported by two wooden blocks. Worn with traditional clothing like yukata and kimono.

examples.japanese: ⟦{浴衣|ゆかた}→浴衣：04081_yukata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{下駄|げた}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}いて→履く：00700_haku⟧⟦{出|で}かけた→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。
examples.english: I went out wearing a yukata and geta.

examples.japanese: {下駄|げた}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧カラコロと⟦{響|ひび}く→響く：00099_hibiku⟧。
examples.english: The sound of geta clogs echoes 'kara-koro'.
examples.notes: カラコロ is onomatopoeia for geta sounds

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏祭|なつまつ}り→夏祭り：09871_natsumatsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{下駄|げた}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Many people wear geta at summer festivals.
When I was a child, I wore geta and played at my grandmother's house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{下駄|げた}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧⟦{機会|きかい}→機会：01302_kikai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}なくなった→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧が、⟦{花火|はなび}→花火：00087_hanabi⟧⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦とき→時：02918_toki⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{浴衣|ゆかた}→浴衣：04081_yukata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{下駄|げた}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出|で}かける→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。
examples.english: These days there are fewer opportunities to wear geta, but I go out in a yukata and geta just for fireworks festivals.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Geta are traditional Japanese footwear, now mainly worn with summer ⟦{浴衣|ゆかた}→浴衣：04081_yukata⟧ at festivals. The distinctive clacking sound they make when walking is culturally evocative.

TYPES:
- ⟦{駒|こま}→駒：noentry⟧{下駄|げた} (standard two-toothed geta)
- ⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{歯|ば}→歯：noentry⟧{下駄|げた} (single-toothed geta, worn by tengu)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {下駄|げた}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{預|あず}ける→預ける：01819_azukeru⟧ (to entrust a decision to someone - lit. 'entrust one's geta')
- {下駄|げた}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}かせる→履く：00700_haku⟧ (to add extra points/pad numbers - lit. 'put geta on')
